title: The Astronaut in Pajamas
summary: When the house goes quiet, Mía's bed turns into a rocket bound for the moon.

scenes.text: Mía put on her softest pajamas and climbed into bed. Outside, the moon glowed round and white above the rooftops. A warm wind moved the curtains slowly, as if it wanted to tell her a secret. Mía closed her eyes for a tiny moment, and when she opened them, her bed was no longer a bed. The sheets were made of silver, the pillow had buttons that twinkled, and two little lights glowed at its tip. Her bed had turned into a soft, cozy rocket, ready to fly.

—Five, four, three, two, one... —whispered Mía, and the rocket lifted off without any loud noise. It rose through the open window, slipped past the curtains, and waved to the sleeping rooftops. Up, high up, the clouds looked like pillows, and the sky was full of stars that winked at her. Mía laughed softly while her flying bed spun among them. She was not afraid at all, because her blanket still covered her, and her teddy bear traveled by her side, peeking out the little rocket window.

The rocket came down slowly and landed on the moon, which was soft as flour. Mía slid out one foot, then the other, and took her first steps on the silver dust. Everything was quiet, a lovely, round kind of quiet. The moon was huge and calm, with gentle mountains and valleys full of light. In every corner, little stars had fallen asleep on the ground, blinking very slowly, like tired lanterns. Mía looked at them tenderly and thought they would be perfect for lighting up her room.

Very carefully, Mía opened her glass jar and began to gather the little stars, one by one. Each time she caught one, the little star let out a tiny laugh, like a giggle of light. Soon the jar filled with golden sparkles dancing inside. Mía did not squeeze them or rush; she gathered them slowly, with gentle fingers, and promised to take care of them. When the jar was full, she closed it softly, so she would not wake them completely. Then she climbed back onto her rocket-bed, hugged her teddy, and turned the ship toward home.

The rocket-bed floated back through the window and settled again in Mía's room, warm and still. She set the jar of little stars beside her pillow, and its soft light filled the room like a kind little lamp. Outside, the moon wished her good night. Mía snuggled under her blanket, closed her sleepy eyes, and breathed very slowly, once, twice. The golden glow hugged her from the inside. And so, among saved-up stars and peaceful dreams, Mía fell fast asleep.
